title: Page the VCF Automation region collection into a stable inventory
prompt:
Platform automation ticket for our VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1 estate. VCF Automation is the successor to vRealize and Aria Automation, and our capacity reports need its full region inventory in a stable order. Build the PowerShell module `VcfaRegionInventory` at the workspace root as `VcfaRegionInventory.psd1` plus `VcfaRegionInventory.psm1`.

VCF Automation ships no PowerCLI cmdlet for this collection, so call it directly over REST. Before implementing, research `queryRegions` in the official Broadcom VCF Automation xAPIs reference. Confirm its method, path, parameters, pagination, response schema, error schema, and authentication requirements, and cite the official sources consulted in the final answer. The only operation in scope is `queryRegions`, `GET /cloudapi/v1/regions`.

Use the installed the `VMware.Sdk.Vcf` PowerCLI SDK family (`VMware.Sdk.Vcf.SddcManager` 13.5.0.25380678 and its `VMware.OpenAPI` dependency). Do not vendor VMware modules or ship binaries. `VcfaRegionInventory.psd1` must set `RootModule` to `VcfaRegionInventory.psm1`, export exactly `Get-VcfaRegion` through `FunctionsToExport`, and declare the estate's PowerCLI baseline in `RequiredModules` as `@{ ModuleName = 'VMware.Sdk.Vcf.SddcManager'; ModuleVersion = '13.5.0.25380678' }`. The module must load cleanly with that SDK present.

Expose this public interface:

`Get-VcfaRegion -ApiEndpoint <uri> -AccessToken <string> [-Filter <string>] [-MetadataFilter <string>] [-SortAsc <string>] [-SortDesc <string>] [-PageSize <int>] [-ApiVersion <string>]`

Requirements:

- `PageSize` defaults to 128, the documented maximum, and must be rejected outside 1..128 before any request is sent. `ApiVersion` defaults to `9.1.0`. `ApiEndpoint` and `AccessToken` are mandatory and non-empty.
- Every request is a `GET` to `/cloudapi/v1/regions` on `ApiEndpoint` with no request body. Send `Authorization: Bearer <AccessToken>` and `Accept: application/json;version=<ApiVersion>`.
- Build the query string in this parameter order: `filter`, `metadata`, `sortAsc`, `sortDesc`, `page`, `pageSize`. `page` and `pageSize` are always present. `Filter`, `MetadataFilter`, `SortAsc` and `SortDesc` map to `filter`, `metadata`, `sortAsc` and `sortDesc` and appear only when the caller bound them; an unset optional parameter is absent from the request target, never sent with an empty value. Percent-encode parameter values.
- Retrieve the collection completely. Always request page 1, then keep requesting the next page while the page just fetched is below the response's `pageCount`, and stop on the last page. A query that matches nothing reports `pageCount` 0 and still costs exactly one request. Never refetch a page and never request a page beyond `pageCount`.
- The service returns pages in its own order and ignores `sortAsc`, so impose the order yourself over the whole accumulated collection: ascending by `name` using ordinal (case-sensitive) comparison, ties broken by ascending ordinal `id`.
- Emit one object per region with properties in this exact order: `Id`, `Name`, `Status`, `LoadBalancerType`, `NsxManagerId`, `SupervisorIds`, `StoragePolicies`, `CpuCapacityMHz`, `MemoryCapacityMiB`. Map them from `id`, `name`, `status`, `loadBalancerType`, `nsxManager.id`, the `id` of each entry of `supervisors` in server order, `storagePolicies` in server order, `cpuCapacityMHz` and `memoryCapacityMiB`.
- Any response other than `200` ends the walk by throwing a class named `VcfaRegionQueryException` exposing `StatusCode` and `MinorErrorCode`. Take `MinorErrorCode` and the exception message detail from the API's `Error` response body. Never put the access token in an exception message.

Acceptance: `pwsh -NoProfile -File verify.ps1`. It verifies the exact method, target, query parameter set and order, headers, paging sequence, emitted order, and omission of every unset optional parameter. Create only `VcfaRegionInventory.psd1` and `VcfaRegionInventory.psm1`.
